title.narrative: Services financiers et techniques intégrés pour l'agriculture

description.narrative:
Smallholder farmers cultivating maize, millet, sorghum with field size lower than 5ha. The project targeting strategy will be oriented to vulnerable people, in particular women, youth and internal displaced people.
1) Number of households a) expected by end of 2025: 200,000 b) expected at project end: 100,000
2) Number of poor and vulnerable households (living on less than USD 15 PPP per capita / day) a) expected by end of 2025: 200,000 b) expected at project end: 100,000

The main objectives of the project are to: - Deploy an insurance solution that would serve as a catalyst for socio-economic development by reducing the vulnerability of smallholder farmers to risks and providing them the financial security to develop their activities, - Improve access to capital for farmers by providing a risk trans-fer solution for MFIs to allocate more capital to the agriculture sector, - Implement technical advisory services that will enable CSA prac-tices and improve the productivity and resilience of smallholder farmers.

The risk of drought is critical and ubiquitous in Burkina Faso, given the variable climatic conditions of the Sahel and the majority of agri-culture in economic activity. According to the Permanent Agricul-tural Survey (EPA), drought affected more than 1 million people on average per year over the period 2004 - 2013 in Burkina Faso. The field study performed by the National Institute of Statistics and De-mography (INSD) revealed that 41% of households in the country are economically affected by rainfall variability annually. The country frequently experiences localised or generalised droughts that affect large regions and impacts agriculture production as well as livestock. Such climate events are recurrent and of high economic severity in nature. They annihilate all development efforts from the populations and perpetually keep them from emerging over the poverty line. More than 40% of the population leave below the poverty line of less than $2 per day. The non-availability of private or public welfare solutions to secure income in adverse circumstances perpetuates the poverty cycle and impedes the emergence of a middle class. The occurrence of a drought event can have a catastrophic effect on socio-economic de-velopment given that close to 90% of the labour force is active in the agriculture value chain.
